title: Cooling-tower fan staging on temperature bands
nl_spec: A cooling tower has two fans that are staged on rising basin-water temperature. Fan1 (lead) runs when the water temperature WaterTemp reaches the lead stage point T_ON1 = 25 C; Fan2 (lag) additionally runs when WaterTemp reaches the lag stage point T_ON2 = 32 C. Staging is monotonic: the lag fan must never run unless the lead fan is also running. The system runs only while Enable is TRUE. EStop is the emergency-stop input, wired normally-closed, so EStop = TRUE means healthy and EStop = FALSE means the emergency stop is ACTIVATED; when it is activated or when Enable is FALSE, both fans must be off. Use pure rising thresholds (no hysteresis / no off-band). Write an IEC 61131-3 Structured Text PROGRAM named cooling_tower with inputs WaterTemp, Enable, EStop and outputs Fan1, Fan2.

interface.name: WaterTemp
interface.description: Basin/return water temperature in deg C

interface.name: EStop
interface.description: Emergency stop, normally-closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = activated

safety_properties.nl: When the emergency stop is activated (EStop = FALSE), both fans are off.
Monotonic staging: the lag fan never runs unless the lead fan is also running.
When the system is disabled (Enable = FALSE), both fans are off.
Positive obligation: while enabled, healthy and at/above the lead stage point, the lead fan runs.

scenarios.description: Boundary staging sweep (healthy and enabled throughout): Fan1 engages at >= 25, Fan2 at >= 32

notes: DRAFT - pending expert PLC review. NEW FAMILY: monotonic capacity-staging ladder (stage N implies stage N-1). Avoids on-delay timing (no timer), bounded counters, mutual exclusion (outputs are nested, not exclusive), hysteresis (pure rising thresholds, no off-band memory), and safety chains. The staging invariant Fan2 -> Fan1 is the structurally novel property class.
